segments.arabic: [711] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا عبد الواحد بن زياد قال: حدثنا عمارة بن القعقاع قال: حدثنا أبو زرعة قال: حدثنا أبو هريرة قال:
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us. He said: ‘Umarah ibn al-Qa‘qa‘ related to us. He said: Abu Zur‘ah related to us. He said: Abu Hurayrah related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يسكت بين التكبير وبين القراءة إسكاتة
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pause silently between the takbir and the recitation.

segments.arabic: قال أحسبه قال هنية
segments.english: He said: I think he said, “briefly.”

segments.arabic: فقلت: بأبي وأمي يا رسول الله إسكاتك بين التكبير والقراءة ما تقول قال أقول اللهم باعد بيني وبين خطاياي كما باعدت بين المشرق والمغرب اللهم نقني من الخطايا كما ينقى الثوب الأبيض من الدنس اللهم اغسل خطاياي بالماء والثلج والبرد
segments.english: I said, “May my father and mother be your ransom, Messenger of Allah. During your silence between the takbir and the recitation, what do you say?” He said, “I say: O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You have put distance between the east and the west. O Allah, cleanse me of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. O Allah, wash away my sins with water, snow and hail.”

notes: The source’s I think he said qualification is preserved without assigning an unnamed speaker. The three complete supplications and their order remain. No additional formula from another prayer opening is supplied.

segments.arabic: [712] حدثنا ابن أبي مريم قال: أخبرنا نافع بن عمر قال: حدثني ابن أبي مليكة عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر
segments.english: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Nafi‘ ibn ‘Umar informed us. He said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah related to me, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ صلى صلاة الكسوف فقام فأطال القيام ثم ركع فأطال الركوع ثم قام فأطال القيام ثم ركع فأطال الركوع ثم رفع ثم سجد فأطال السجود ثم رفع ثم سجد فأطال السجود ثم قام فأطال القيام ثم ركع فأطال الركوع ثم رفع فأطال القيام ثم ركع فأطال الركوع ثم رفع فسجد فأطال السجود ثم رفع ثم سجد فأطال السجود ثم انصرف، فقال قد دنت مني الجنة حتى لو اجترأت عليها لجئتكم بقطاف من قطافها ودنت مني النار حتى قلت: أي رب وأنا معهم فإذا امرأة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed the eclipse prayer. He stood and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he stood and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he rose, then prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he rose, then prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he stood and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he rose and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he rose and prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he rose, then prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he finished and said: “Paradise came so close to me that, had I ventured towards it, I would have brought you a cluster from its clusters. The Fire came so close to me that I said, ‘O my Lord, am I among them?’ Then there was a woman.”

segments.arabic: حسبت أنه قال
segments.english: I think he said:

segments.arabic: تخدشها هرة قلت: ما شأن هذه قالوا حبستها حتى ماتت جوعا لا أطعمتها ولا أرسلتها تأكل
segments.english: “A cat was scratching her. I said, ‘What is the matter with this woman?’ They said, ‘She confined it until it died of hunger. She neither fed it nor let it go to eat.’”

segments.arabic: قال نافع حسبت أنه قال من خشيش أو خشاش الأرض
segments.english: Nafi‘ said: I think he said, “From the earth’s khashish, or khashash.”

notes: Every repeated standing, bowing, rising and prostration remains in source order. Both uncertainty phrases and the closing two lexical forms remain. segments.arabic: [713] حدثنا موسى قال: حدثنا عبد الواحد قال: حدثنا الأعمش عن عمارة بن عمير عن أبي معمر قال
segments.english: Musa related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: al-A‘mash related to us, from ‘Umarah ibn ‘Umayr, from Abu Ma‘mar, who said:

segments.arabic: قلنا لخباب أكان رسول الله ﷺ يقرأ في الظهر والعصر قال: نعم قلنا بم كنتم تعرفون ذاك قال باضطراب لحيته

segments.arabic: [714] حدثنا حجاج حدثنا شعبة قال: أنبأنا أبو إسحاق قال: سمعت عبد الله بن يزيد يخطب قال: حدثنا البراء وكان غير كذوب

segments.english: When they prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he raised his head from bowing, they remained standing until they saw that he had prostrated.

segments.arabic: [715] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء بن يسار عن عبد الله بن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: خسفت الشمس على عهد رسول الله ﷺ فصلى قالوا يا رسول الله رأيناك تناول شيئا في مقامك ثم رأيناك تكعكعت قال إني أريت الجنة فتناولت منها عنقودا ولو أخذته لأكلتم منه ما بقيت الدنيا
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he prayed. They said, “Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something in the place where you stood, then we saw you move back.” He said, “I was shown Paradise and reached for a cluster from it. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remained.”

segments.arabic: [716] حدثنا محمد بن سنان قال: حدثنا فليح قال: حدثنا هلال بن علي عن أنس بن مالك قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us. He said: Fulayh related to us. He said: Hilal ibn ‘Ali related to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى لنا النبي ﷺ ثم رقي المنبر فأشار بيديه قبل قبلة المسجد، ثم قال لقد رأيت الآن منذ صليت لكم الصلاة الجنة والنار ممثلتين في قبلة هذا الجدار فلم أر كاليوم في الخير والشر ثلاثا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in prayer, then ascended the pulpit and gestured with both hands towards the mosque’s direction of prayer. Then he said, “Just now, since I led you in prayer, I saw Paradise and the Fire represented on the prayer-facing side of this wall. I have never seen the like of today in good and evil”—three times.

notes: Both hands, the pulpit, the wall and the final three-times qualification remain. The selected text says since I prayed for you, not an added claim that this happened only at the moment the prayer began. The note three times is not expanded into three invented repeated quotations.

segments.arabic: [717] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: أخبرنا يحيى بن سعيد قال: حدثنا ابن أبي عروبة قال: حدثنا قتادة أن أنس بن مالك حدثهم قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id informed us. He said: Ibn Abi ‘Arubah related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us that Anas ibn Malik related to them. He said:

segments.arabic: قال النبي ﷺ ما بال أقوام يرفعون أبصارهم إلى السماء في صلاتهم فاشتد قوله في ذلك حتى قال لينتهن عن ذلك أو لتخطفن أبصارهم
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “What is the matter with people who raise their eyes towards the sky during their prayer?” His words about this grew stern until he said, “They must stop doing that, or their eyesight will be snatched away.”

notes: The complete selected chain uses informed us for Yahya; the historical print uses related to us. The change in tone and both alternatives in the warning remain.

segments.arabic: [718] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا أبو الأحوص قال: حدثنا أشعث بن سليم عن أبيه عن مسروق عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu al-Ahwas related to us. He said: Ash‘ath ibn Sulaym related to us, from his father, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: سألت رسول الله ﷺ عن الالتفات في الصلاة، فقال هو اختلاس يختلسه الشيطان من صلاة العبد
segments.english: I asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about turning around during prayer. He said, “It is a theft that Satan steals from the servant’s prayer.”

notes: The selected answer explicitly describes a theft from the servant’s prayer. It is not replaced by a broader paraphrase about people’s prayers.

segments.arabic: [719] حدثنا قتيبة قال: حدثنا سفيان عن الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة
segments.english: Qutaybah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ صلى في خميصة لها أعلام، فقال شغلتني أعلام هذه اذهبوا بها إلى أبي جهم وأتوني بأنبجانية
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in a patterned cloak. He said, “Its patterns distracted me. Take it to Abu Jahm and bring me a plain garment.”

notes: Khamisah and inbijaniyah are rendered as patterned cloak and plain garment. The source does not explicitly add from him after the request for the plain garment; that expansion is not imported from the Khan-family comparison.

segments.arabic: [720] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا ليث عن نافع عن ابن عمر
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Layth related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

segments.arabic: أنه رأى النبي ﷺ نخامة في قبلة المسجد وهو يصلي بين يدي الناس فحتها، ثم قال حين انصرف إن أحدكم إذا كان في الصلاة فإن الله قبل وجهه فلا يتنخمن أحد قبل وجهه في الصلاة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm on the mosque’s prayer-facing side while he was praying in front of the people, and scraped it away. Then, when he finished, he said, “When one of you is in prayer, Allah is before his face. So no one should spit phlegm in front of his face during prayer.”

segments.arabic: رواه موسى بن عقبة وابن أبي رواد عن نافع
segments.english: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah and Ibn Abi Rawwad related it from Nafi‘.

notes: Both closing transmission routes remain. Bewley abbreviates the closing material to Nafi; the Khan-family body omits it. The digital chapter heading has قي القبلة where both prints have في القبلة; its English heading is withheld, while the unchanged digital heading and the two printed readings remain available.

segments.arabic: [721] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا ليث بن سعد عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني أنس قال
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Layth ibn Sa‘d related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Anas informed me. He said:

segments.arabic: بينما المسلمون في صلاة الفجر لم يفجأهم إلا رسول الله ﷺ كشف ستر حجرة عائشة فنظر إليهم وهم صفوف فتبسم يضحك ونكص أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه على عقبيه ليصل له الصف فظن أنه يريد الخروج وهم المسلمون أن يفتتنوا في صلاتهم فأشار إليهم أتموا صلاتكم فأرخى الستر وتوفي من آخر ذلك اليوم
segments.english: While the Muslims were in the dawn prayer, they were suddenly surprised by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lifting the curtain of ‘A’ishah’s room. He looked at them as they stood in rows and smiled with laughter. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, stepped backwards to join the row, thinking that he wanted to come out. The Muslims were on the verge of being distracted from their prayer. He gestured to them, “Complete your prayer.” Then he lowered the curtain, and he died later that day.

notes: The complete Anas introduction, Abu Bakr honorific, gesture, lowered curtain and later-that-day statement remain. Historical reconciliation is not inserted into the selected report.

segments.arabic: [722] حدثنا موسى قال: حدثنا أبو عوانة قال: حدثنا عبد الملك بن عمير عن جابر بن سمرة قال
segments.english: Musa related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr related to us, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said:

segments.arabic: شكا أهل الكوفة سعدا إلى عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه فعزله واستعمل عليهم عمارا فشكوا حتى ذكروا انه لا يحسن يصلي فأرسل إليه، فقال: يا أبا إسحاق إن هؤلاء يزعمون أنك لا تحسن تصلي قال أبو إسحاق أما أنا والله فإني كنت أصلي بهم صلاة رسول الله ﷺ ما أخرم عنها أصلي صلاة العشاء فأركد في الأوليين وأخف في الأخريين قال ذاك الظن بك يا أبا إسحاق فأرسل معه رجلا أو رجالا إلى الكوفة فسأل عنه أهل الكوفة ولم يدع مسجدا إلا سأل عنه ويثنون معروفا حتى دخل مسجدا لبني عبس فقام رجل منهم يقال له أسامة بن قتادة يكنى أبا سعدة قال: أما إذ نشدتنا فإن سعدا كان لا يسير بالسرية ولا يقسم بالسوية ولا يعدل في القضية قال سعد أما والله لأدعون بثلاث اللهم إن كان عبدك هذا كاذبا قام رياء وسمعة فأطل عمره وأطل فقره وعرضه بالفتن وكان بعد إذا سئل يقول شيخ كبير مفتون أصابتني دعوة سعد
segments.english: The people of Kufah complained about Sa‘d to ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, so he removed him and appointed ‘Ammar over them. Their complaints went so far as to say that he did not know how to pray properly. He sent for him and said, “Abu Ishaq, these people claim that you do not know how to pray properly.” Abu Ishaq said, “As for me, by Allah, I used to lead them in the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, without falling short of it. I would pray the night prayer, taking my time in the first two rak‘ahs and making the last two brief.” He said, “That is what we thought of you, Abu Ishaq.” He sent a man—or men—with him to Kufah, and asked the people of Kufah about him. He left no mosque without asking about him, and they spoke well of him, until he entered a mosque of Banu ‘Abs. A man among them called Usamah ibn Qatadah, known as Abu Sa‘dah, stood and said, “Since you have asked us under oath, Sa‘d does not go out with the military expedition, does not divide equally, and does not judge justly.” Sa‘d said, “By Allah, I will pray for three things: O Allah, if this servant of Yours is lying and stood up to show off and seek reputation, prolong his life, prolong his poverty, and expose him to trials.” Afterwards, when he was asked, he would say, “An old man afflicted with trials; Sa‘d’s prayer has struck me.”

segments.arabic: قال عبد الملك فأنا رأيته بعد قد سقط حاجباه على عينيه من الكبر وإنه ليتعرض للجواري في الطرق يغمزهن
segments.english: ‘Abd al-Malik said: I saw him afterwards, when his eyebrows had fallen over his eyes from old age. He would accost young girls in the streets and pinch them.

notes: The selected man or men uncertainty is retained rather than converted to a couple of men. Both showing off and seeking reputation remain. The entire closing observation is attributed to Abd al-Malik and kept separate from the preceding account. The source names the night prayer here; the separately printed 724b account instead names the two afternoon prayers.

segments.arabic: [723] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا الزهري عن محمود بن الربيع عن عبادة بن الصامت
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: al-Zuhri related to us, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, from ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “There is no prayer for one who does not recite the Opening of the Book.”

notes: The statement remains no prayer, without replacing it with the explicit legal paraphrase invalid from an English comparison.

segments.arabic: [724] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا يحيى عن عبيد الله قال: حدثني سعيد بن أبي سعيد عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, who said: Sa‘id ibn Abi Sa‘id related to me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ دخل المسجد فدخل رجل فصلى فسلم على النبي ﷺ فرد، وقال ارجع فصل فإنك لم تصل فرجع يصلي كما صلى ثم جاء فسلم على النبي ﷺ، فقال ارجع فصل فإنك لم تصل ثلاثا، فقال والذي بعثك بالحق ما أحسن غيره فعلمني، فقال إذا قمت إلى الصلاة فكبر ثم اقرأ ما تيسر معك من القرآن ثم اركع حتى تطمئن راكعا ثم ارفع حتى تعتدل قائما ثم اسجد حتى تطمئن ساجدا ثم ارفع حتى تطمئن جالسا وافعل ذلك في صلاتك كلها
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the mosque. A man entered and prayed, then greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He returned the greeting and said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed.” He went back and prayed as he had prayed before. Then he came and greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed”—three times. He said, “By the One who sent you with the truth, I know no better than this, so teach me.” He said, “When you stand for prayer, say the takbir, then recite whatever is easy for you of the Quran. Then bow until you are at rest while bowing. Then rise until you stand upright. Then prostrate until you are at rest while prostrating. Then rise until you are at rest while sitting. Do that throughout your prayer.”

notes: The two written return commands and the qualification three times remain in source order. No third quotation is invented, and none of the successive postures or settling instructions is omitted.

segments.arabic: حدثنا أبو النعمان حدثنا أبو عوانة عن عبد الملك بن عمير عن جابر بن سمرة قال قال سعد
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: Sa‘d said:

segments.arabic: وكنت أصلي بهم صلاة رسول الله ﷺ صلاتي العشي لا أخرم عنها أركد في الأوليين وأحذف في الأخريين فقال عمر رضي الله عنه ذلك الظن بك
segments.english: I used to lead them in the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the two afternoon prayers, without falling short of it: I would take my time in the first two rak‘ahs and make the last two brief. ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “That is what we thought of you.”

Its heading falls before this report; the modern heading falls after it. Neither variant nor placement is silently reconciled. segments.arabic: [725] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا شيبان عن يحيى عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه قال:
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يقرأ في الركعتين الأوليين من صلاة الظهر بفاتحة الكتاب وسورتين يطول في الأولى ويقصر في الثانية ويسمع الآية أحيانا وكان يقرأ في العصر بفاتحة الكتاب وسورتين وكان يطول في الأولى وكان يطول في الركعة الأولى من صلاة الصبح ويقصر في الثانية
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Opening of the Book and two surahs in the first two rak‘ahs of the noon prayer, making the first longer and the second shorter. Sometimes he would make a verse audible. In the afternoon prayer he would recite the Opening of the Book and two surahs, and would make the first longer. In the dawn prayer he would make the first rak‘ah longer and the second shorter.

comparisons.note: Bewley reference 725 contains both the Sa‘d and Abu Qatadah reports. This record identifies only the corresponding complete part; both full Arabic chains remain separately represented.

notes: The selected and historical-print clause making the first longer during Asr is retained; the modern print and Bewley comparison omit that clause here. Bewley 725 part two is this account, while part one is the separate report now identified as app reference 724b.

segments.arabic: [726] حدثنا عمر بن حفص قال: حدثنا أبي قال: حدثنا الأعمش حدثني عمارة عن أبي معمر قال
segments.english: ‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: al-A‘mash related to us. ‘Umarah related to me, from Abu Ma‘mar, who said:

segments.arabic: سألنا خبابا أكان النبي ﷺ يقرأ في الظهر والعصر قال: نعم قلنا بأي شيء كنتم تعرفون قال باضطراب لحيته
segments.english: We asked Khabbab, “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the noon and afternoon prayers?” He said, “Yes.” We said, “How did you recognize that?” He said, “By the movement of his beard.”

notes: The source’s plural we asked remains. This is a separate complete chain and report from 727, whose selected questions are singular.

segments.arabic: [727] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال: حدثنا سفيان عن الأعمش عن عمارة بن عمير عن أبي معمر قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A‘mash, from ‘Umarah ibn ‘Umayr, from Abu Ma‘mar, who said:

segments.arabic: قلت لخباب بن الأرت أكان النبي ﷺ يقرأ في الظهر والعصر قال: نعم قال: قلت: بأي شيء كنتم تعلمون قراءته قال باضطراب لحيته
segments.english: I said to Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the noon and afternoon prayers?” He said, “Yes.” He said: I said, “How did you know that he was reciting?” He said, “By the movement of his beard.”

notes: The singular I said and the full selected Prophet wording remain; they are not replaced by the plural and Messenger wording in Bewley.

segments.arabic: [728] حدثنا المكي بن إبراهيم عن هشام عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه قال:
segments.english: Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim related to us, from Hisham, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يقرأ في الركعتين من الظهر والعصر بفاتحة الكتاب وسورة سورة ويسمعنا الآية أحيانا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Opening of the Book and a surah in each of the two rak‘ahs of the noon and afternoon prayers. Sometimes he would make a verse audible to us.

notes: The father is the father of Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah in the complete chain, not Abu Qatadah’s father as the abbreviated Bewley opening states. Surah surah is distributed as a surah in each, rather than two surahs in one rakah.

segments.arabic: [729] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: إن أم الفضل سمعته وهو يقرأ والمرسلات عرفا فقالت: يا بني والله لقد ذكرتني بقراءتك هذه السورة إنها لآخر ما سمعت من رسول الله ﷺ يقرأ بها في المغرب
segments.english: Umm al-Fadl heard him reciting “Wa-l-mursalati ‘urfa” and said, “My son, by Allah, your recitation of this surah has reminded me: it was the last one I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the sunset prayer.”

notes: The short Quranic identifier is transliterated, without adding the full surah or an external verse translation. The complete selected chain and dual honorific remain.

segments.arabic: [730] حدثنا أبو عاصم عن ابن جريج عن ابن أبي مليكة عن عروة بن الزبير عن مروان بن الحكم قال:
segments.english: Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who said:

segments.arabic: قال لي زيد بن ثابت ما لك تقرأ في المغرب بقصار وقد سمعت النبي ﷺ يقرأ بطولى الطوليين
segments.english: Zayd ibn Thabit said to me, “Why do you recite short surahs in the sunset prayer, when I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite the longer of the two long ones?”

notes: The source does not name either of the two long surahs. Al-Araf and al-Mufassal are not inserted from commentary or the English comparison. Brill adds min al-mufassal and fiha; these are absent from the selected digital and modern wording.

segments.arabic: [731] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم عن أبيه قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut‘im, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ قرأ في المغرب بالطور
segments.english: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite al-Tur in the sunset prayer.

notes: The selected chain makes Muhammad’s father the speaker of I heard. It is preserved in full, without adding another my father attribution inside the report from the Khan-family comparison.

segments.arabic: [732] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا معتمر عن أبيه عن بكر عن أبي رافع قال
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir related to us, from his father, from Bakr, from Abu Rafi‘, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت مع أبي هريرة العتمة فقرأ إذا السماء انشقت فسجد فقلت له قال سجدت خلف أبي القاسم ﷺ فلا أزال أسجد بها حتى ألقاه
segments.english: I prayed the night prayer with Abu Hurayrah. He recited “Idha al-sama’u inshaqqat” and prostrated. I spoke to him. He said, “I prostrated behind Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I will continue to prostrate on reciting it until I meet him.”

notes: The selected and modern text say I spoke to him without giving the content of the question. What is this is not imported from Brill or from the separate 734 report. Atamah is rendered night prayer.

segments.arabic: [733] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة عن عدي قال: سمعت البراء
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Adi, who said: I heard al-Bara’:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان في سفر فقرأ في العشاء في إحدى الركعتين بالتين والزيتون
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was travelling and recited “al-Tin wa-l-zaytun” in one of the two rak‘ahs of the night prayer.

notes: The selected one of the two is not changed to the first. The full opening Quranic phrase remains as a transliterated identifier.

segments.arabic: [734] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يزيد بن زريع قال: حدثني التيمي عن بكر عن أبي رافع قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us. He said: al-Taymi related to me, from Bakr, from Abu Rafi‘, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت مع أبي هريرة العتمة فقرأ إذا السماء انشقت فسجد فقلت: ما هذه قال سجدت بها خلف أبي القاسم ﷺ فلا أزال أسجد بها حتى ألقاه
segments.english: I prayed the night prayer with Abu Hurayrah. He recited “Idha al-sama’u inshaqqat” and prostrated. I said, “What is this?” He said, “I prostrated on reciting it behind Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I will continue to prostrate on reciting it until I meet him.”

segments.arabic: [735] حدثنا خلاد بن يحيى قال: حدثنا مسعر قال: حدثنا عدي بن ثابت سمع البراء رضى الله تعالى عنه قال:
segments.english: Khallad ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Mis‘ar related to us. He said: ‘Adi ibn Thabit related to us that he heard al-Bara’, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say:

segments.arabic: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقرأ والتين والزيتون في العشاء وما سمعت أحدا أحسن صوتا منه أو قراءة
segments.english: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite “Wa-l-tini wa-l-zaytun” in the night prayer. I have not heard anyone with a more beautiful voice than his—or recitation.

notes: The alternative voice or recitation is retained rather than converted to an unqualified pair of claims. The source honorific remains in the chain.

segments.arabic: [736] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي عون قال: سمعت جابر بن سمرة قال:
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu ‘Awn, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah say:

segments.arabic: قال عمر لسعد لقد شكوك في كل شيء حتى الصلاة قال: أما أنا فأمد في الأوليين وأحذف في الأخريين ولا آلو ما اقتديت به من صلاة رسول الله ﷺ قال: صدقت ذاك الظن بك أو ظني بك
segments.english: ‘Umar said to Sa‘d, “They have complained about you in everything, even the prayer.” He said, “As for me, I prolong the first two rak‘ahs and make the last two brief, and I spare no effort to follow the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” He said, “You have spoken the truth. That is what we thought of you—or what I thought of you.”

notes: Both alternative closing formulations remain. The source’s statement about sparing no effort is not replaced with a stronger claim of flawless imitation.

segments.arabic: [737] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا سيار بن سلامة قال
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Sayyar ibn Salamah related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: دخلت أنا وأبي على أبي برزة الأسلمي فسألناه عن وقت الصلوات، فقال: كان النبي ﷺ يصلي الظهر حين تزول الشمس والعصر ويرجع الرجل إلى أقصى المدينة والشمس حية
segments.english: My father and I visited Abu Barzah al-Aslami and asked him about the times of the prayers. He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer when the sun declined, and the afternoon prayer when a man could return to the furthest part of Madinah while the sun was still bright.

segments.arabic: ونسيت ما قال في المغرب
segments.english: I have forgotten what he said about the sunset prayer.

segments.arabic: ولا يبالي بتأخير العشاء إلى ثلث الليل ولا يحب النوم قبلها ولا الحديث بعدها ويصلي الصبح فينصرف الرجل فيعرف جليسه وكان يقرأ في الركعتين أو إحداهما ما بين الستين إلى المائة
segments.english: He did not mind delaying the night prayer until a third of the night. He did not like sleeping before it or conversation afterwards. He would pray the dawn prayer and a man would leave able to recognize the person sitting beside him. He used to recite between sixty and a hundred in the two rak‘ahs—or in one of them.

notes: The forgetting remark remains separate from the prayer description; Ibn Hajar attributes it to Sayyar. The selected did not mind is retained rather than substituted with the preference wording in Bewley. The two rakahs or one uncertainty and sixty to a hundred range remain; the source has no explicit noun verses after the count.

segments.arabic: [738] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن إبراهيم قال: أخبرنا ابن جريج قال: أخبرني عطاء أنه سمع أبا هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه يقول:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: ‘Ata’ informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say:

segments.arabic: في كل صلاة يقرأ فما أسمعنا رسول الله ﷺ أسمعناكم وما أخفى عنا أخفينا عنكم وإن لم تزد على أم القرآن أجزأت وإن زدت فهو خير
segments.english: There is recitation in every prayer. What the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, made audible to us, we make audible to you; and what he kept quiet from us, we keep quiet from you. If you recite no more than the Mother of the Quran, it is sufficient; and if you recite more, it is better.

notes: This is Abu Hurayrah’s statement, not a direct quotation assigned to the Prophet. The selected Mother of the Quran designation is retained.

segments.arabic: [739] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا أبو عوانة عن أبي بشر عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: انطلق النبي ﷺ في طائفة من أصحابه عامدين إلى سوق عكاظ وقد حيل بين الشياطين وبين خبر السماء وأرسلت عليهم الشهب فرجعت الشياطين إلى قومهم فقالوا مالكم فقالوا حيل بيننا وبين خبر السماء وأرسلت علينا الشهب قالوا ما حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء إلا شيء حدث فاضربوا مشارق الأرض ومغاربها فانظروا ما هذا الذي حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء فانصرف أولئك الذين توجهوا نحو تهامة إلى النبي ﷺ وهو بنخلة عامدين إلى سوق عكاظ وهو يصلي بأصحابه صلاة الفجر فلما سمعوا القرآن استمعوا له فقالوا هذا والله الذي حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء فهنالك حين رجعوا إلى قومهم فقالوا يا قومنا { إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا } فأنزل الله على نبيه ﷺ { قل أوحي إلي }
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out with a group of his companions, heading for the market of ‘Ukaz. The devils had been kept from the news of heaven, and shooting stars had been sent against them. The devils returned to their people, who said, “What is the matter with you?” They said, “We have been kept from the news of heaven, and shooting stars have been sent against us.” They said, “Nothing has come between you and the news of heaven except something that has happened. Travel to the eastern and western parts of the earth, and see what it is that has come between you and the news of heaven.” Those who headed towards Tihamah came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was at Nakhlah, heading for the market of ‘Ukaz, and was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Quran, they listened to it and said, “By Allah, this is what has come between you and the news of heaven.” Then, when they returned to their people, they said, “Our people, ‘We have heard a wondrous Quran, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.’” Allah then revealed to His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “Say: It has been revealed to me.”

segments.arabic: وإنما أوحي إليه قول الجن
segments.english: Only the words of the jinn were revealed to him.

notes: The digital narrator name سعد بن جبير is explicitly corrected to سعيد بن جبير on the agreement of both prints. The original remains retained. The selected you in the second news-of-heaven statement is also printed in both witnesses; it is not silently changed to us as in the English comparisons. Only the Quranic fragments actually present are translated. The closing statement about what was revealed remains separately marked.

segments.arabic: [740] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثنا أيوب عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: قرأ النبي ﷺ فيما أمر وسكت فيما أمر { وما كان ربك نسيا } { لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة }
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited where he was commanded and remained silent where he was commanded. “Your Lord is never forgetful.” “You have indeed had a good example in the Messenger of Allah.”

notes: The selected recited and remained silent are not expanded inside the hadith to specify kinds of prayer. Both Quranic fragments are retained without adding surrounding verses.

segments.arabic: [741] وقال عبيد الله عن ثابت عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: ‘Ubaydullah said, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: كان رجل من الأنصار يؤمهم في مسجد قباء وكان كلما افتتح سورة يقرأ بها لهم في الصلاة مما يقرأ به افتتح قل هوالله أحد حتى يفرغ منها ثم يقرأ سورة أخرى معها وكان يصنع ذلك في كل ركعة فكلمه أصحابه فقالوا إنك تفتتح بهذه السورة ثم لا ترى أنها تجزئك حتى تقرأ بأخرى فإما تقرأ بها وإما أن تدعها وتقرأ بأخرى، فقال: ما أنا بتاركها إن أحببتم أن أؤمكم بذلك فعلت وإن كرهتم تركتكم وكانوا يرون أنه من أفضلهم وكرهوا أن يؤمهم غيره فلما أتاهم النبي ﷺ أخبروه الخبر، فقال: يا فلان ما يمنعك أن تفعل ما يأمرك به أصحابك وما يحملك على لزوم هذه السورة في كل ركعة، فقال إني أحبها، فقال حبك إياها أدخلك الجنة
segments.english: A man of the Ansar used to lead them in prayer in the mosque of Quba’. Whenever he began a surah to recite for them during the prayer, he began with “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” until he finished it, then recited another surah with it. He did this in every rak‘ah. His companions spoke to him, saying, “You begin with this surah, then you do not consider it sufficient until you recite another. Either recite it, or leave it and recite another.” He said, “I will not leave it. If you would like me to lead you in prayer in this way, I will do so; and if you dislike it, I will leave you.” They considered him one of the best of them, and did not want anyone else to lead them. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to them, they told him what had happened. He said, “So-and-so, what prevents you from doing what your companions ask you to do, and what makes you persist in this surah in every rak‘ah?” He said, “I love it.” He said, “Your love for it has admitted you to the Garden.”

segments.arabic: [742] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة عن عمرو بن مرة قال: سمعت أبا وائل قال
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abu Wa’il say:

segments.arabic: جاء رجل إلى بن مسعود، فقال قرأت المفصل الليلة في ركعة، فقال هذا كهذ الشعر لقد عرفت النظائر التي كان النبي ﷺ يقرن بينهن فذكر عشرين سورة من المفصل سورتين في كل ركعة
segments.english: A man came to Ibn Mas‘ud and said, “I recited the Mufassal last night in one rak‘ah.” He said, “Rattling it off like poetry! I know the comparable surahs that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pair together.” He then mentioned twenty surahs of the Mufassal, two surahs in each rak‘ah.

notes: The printed vowel marks identify هذًّا كهذّ الشعر as rapid recitation like poetry. The selected and historical text have two surahs in each rakah; the modern print adds two from the Ha Mim group. That addition, also reflected in the Khan-family comparison, is documented rather than inserted.

segments.arabic: [743] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا همام عن يحيى عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان يقرأ في الظهر في الأوليين بأم الكتاب وسورتين وفي الركعتين الأخريين بأم الكتاب ويسمعنا الآية ويطول في الركعة الأولى مالا يطول في الركعة الثانية وهكذا في العصر وهكذا في الصبح
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Mother of the Book and two surahs in the first two rak‘ahs of the noon prayer, and the Mother of the Book in the last two rak‘ahs. He would make a verse audible to us, and prolong the first rak‘ah more than the second. It was likewise in the afternoon prayer, and likewise in the dawn prayer.

notes: The selected Mother of the Book designation remains. Sometimes is absent here and is not imported from either English comparison or report 745. The closing likewise statements remain without an explanation that could imply four rakahs for the dawn prayer.

segments.arabic: [744] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا جرير عن الأعمش عن عمارة بن عمير عن أبي معمر
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from al-A‘mash, from ‘Umarah ibn ‘Umayr, from Abu Ma‘mar:

segments.arabic: قلت لخباب أكان رسول الله ﷺ يقرأ في الظهر والعصر قال: نعم قلنا من أين علمت قال باضطراب لحيته
segments.english: I said to Khabbab, “Did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the noon and afternoon prayers?” He said, “Yes.” We said, “How did you know?” He said, “By the movement of his beard.”

notes: The selected singular I said followed by plural We said remains. The first question is not made plural as in the Khan-family comparison.

segments.arabic: [745] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف حدثنا الأوزاعي حدثني يحيى بن أبي كثير حدثني عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. Al-Awza‘i related to us. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to me. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah related to me, from his father:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان يقرأ بأم الكتاب وسورة معها في الركعتين الأوليين من صلاة الظهر وصلاة العصر ويسمعنا الآية أحيانا وكان يطيل في الركعة الأولى
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Mother of the Book and a surah with it in the first two rak‘ahs of the noon and afternoon prayers. Sometimes he would make a verse audible to us. He used to prolong the first rak‘ah.

notes: Both related to me verbs are retained. The source explicitly says sometimes here, unlike 743.

segments.arabic: [747] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن سعيد بن المسيب وأبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن أنهما أخبراه عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, who both informed him, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ قال: إذا أمن الإمام فأمنوا فإنه من وافق تأمينه تأمين الملائكة غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه،
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When the imam says Amin, say Amin, for whoever’s saying of Amin coincides with the angels’ saying of Amin will have his previous sins forgiven.”

segments.arabic: وقال ابن شهاب وكان رسول الله ﷺ يقول: آمين
segments.english: Ibn Shihab said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say, “Amin.”

notes: Both named transmitters and both informed him remain in the chain. The Ibn Shihab closing statement remains separately attributed, with its own honorific. The historical print says Messenger of Allah in the opening report; the selected and modern print say Prophet.

segments.arabic: [748] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إذا قال أحدكم آمين وقالت الملائكة في السماء آمين فوافقت إحداهما الأخرى غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When one of you says Amin and the angels in heaven say Amin, and one coincides with the other, his previous sins are forgiven.”

notes: The full selected chain and companion honorific remain. This complete report stays distinct from the neighbouring accounts.

segments.arabic: [749] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن سمي مولى أبي بكر عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إذا قال الإمام { غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين } فقولوا آمين فإنه من وافق قوله قول الملائكة غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When the imam says, ‘Not those upon whom there is anger, nor those who have gone astray,’ say Amin, for whoever’s words coincide with the angels’ words will have his previous sins forgiven.”

segments.arabic: تابعه محمد بن عمرو عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ ونعيم المجمر عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Amr followed him in relating it, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; and Nu‘aym al-Mujmir, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him.

notes: The complete two closing routes remain, including Muhammad ibn Amr, which the Bewley comparison abbreviates away. The Khan-family body omits both routes and adds interpretive group names to the Quranic fragment; none of those additions enter the selected translation. Mawla is rendered freedman here; the source’s short Abu Bakr name is not expanded.

segments.arabic: [750] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا همام عن الأعلم وهو زياد عن الحسن عن أبي بكرة
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from al-A‘lam—who is Ziyad—from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah:

segments.arabic: أنه انتهى إلى النبي ﷺ وهو راكع فركع قبل أن يصل إلى الصف فذكر ذلك للنبي ﷺ، فقال زادك الله حرصا ولا تعد
segments.english: He reached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was bowing, and bowed before he reached the row. He mentioned this to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “May Allah increase your eagerness, but do not do it again.”

notes: The selected third-person narration and the identification al-Alam, who is Ziyad, remain. The wording is not expanded to identify exactly which action the last instruction concerns.

segments.arabic: [751] حدثنا إسحاق الواسطي قال: حدثنا خالد عن الجريري عن أبي العلاء عن مطرف عن عمران بن حصين قال
segments.english: Ishaq al-Wasiti related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-‘Ala’, from Mutarrif, from ‘Imran ibn Husayn, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى مع علي رضى الله تعالى عنه بالبصرة، فقال: ذكرنا هذا الرجل صلاة كنا نصليها مع رسول الله ﷺ فذكر أنه كان يكبر كلما رفع وكلما وضع
segments.english: He prayed with ‘Ali, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, in Basrah, and said, “This man has reminded us of a prayer we used to pray with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” He mentioned that he would say the takbir whenever he rose and whenever he lowered himself.

notes: The selected short narrator names are not expanded. The repeated whenever and third-person framing remain.

segments.arabic: [752] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أنه كان يصلي بهم فيكبر كلما خفض ورفع فإذا انصرف قال إني لأشبهكم صلاة برسول الله ﷺ
segments.english: He used to lead them in prayer, saying the takbir whenever he lowered himself or rose. When he finished, he said, “My prayer resembles the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more closely than that of any of you.”

segments.arabic: [753] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا حماد عن غيلان بن جرير عن مطرف بن عبد الله قال
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Mutarrif ibn ‘Abdullah, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت خلف علي بن أبي طالب رضى الله تعالى عنه أنا وعمران بن حصين فكان إذا سجد كبر وإذا رفع رأسه كبر وإذا نهض من الركعتين كبر فلما قضى الصلاة أخذ بيدي عمران بن حصين، فقال قد ذكرني هذا صلاة محمد ﷺ أو قال لقد صلى بنا صلاة محمد ﷺ
segments.english: ‘Imran ibn Husayn and I prayed behind ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. When he prostrated, he said the takbir; when he raised his head, he said the takbir; and when he rose after the two rak‘ahs, he said the takbir. When he finished the prayer, ‘Imran ibn Husayn took my hand and said, “This has reminded me of the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace”—or he said, “He has led us in the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: Both alternative closing formulations and both honorifics remain. The selected short Hammad name is not expanded from the historical print.

segments.arabic: [754] حدثنا عمرو بن عون قال: حدثنا هشيم عن أبي بشر عن عكرمة قال:
segments.english: ‘Amr ibn ‘Awn related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, from ‘Ikrimah, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رجلا عند المقام يكبر في كل خفض ورفع وإذا قام وإذا وضع فأخبرت بن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال أو ليس تلك صلاة النبي ﷺ لا أم لك
segments.english: I saw a man at the Maqam saying the takbir at every lowering and rising, when he stood and when he lowered himself. I informed Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. He said, “Is that not the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace? May you have no mother!”

notes: The full concluding Arabic expression remains in a literal working rendering, with Ibn Hajar’s explanation separately cited as context. The Khan-family body paraphrases it as admonished me. The source’s Maqam is not expanded inside the report.

segments.arabic: [755] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: أخبرنا همام عن قتادة عن عكرمة قال
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam informed us, from Qatadah, from ‘Ikrimah, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت خلف شيخ بمكة فكبر ثنتين وعشرين تكبيرة فقلت لابن عباس إنه أحمق، فقال ثكلتك أمك سنة أبي القاسم ﷺ،
segments.english: I prayed behind an old man in Makkah, and he said the takbir twenty-two times. I said to Ibn ‘Abbas, “He is foolish.” He said, “May your mother be bereaved of you! The practice of Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

segments.arabic: وقال موسى حدثنا أبان حدثنا قتادة حدثنا عكرمة
segments.english: Musa said: Aban related to us. Qatadah related to us. ‘Ikrimah related to us.

segments.arabic: [756] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني أبو بكر ابن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث أنه سمع أبا هريرة يقول
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah say:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا قام إلى الصلاة يكبر حين يقوم ثم يكبر حين يركع ثم يقول سمع الله لمن حمده حين يرفع صلبه من الركعة ثم يقول وهو قائم ربنا لك الحمد
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood for prayer, he would say the takbir as he stood, then say the takbir as he bowed. Then he would say, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” as he raised his back from bowing. Then, while standing, he would say, “Our Lord, to You belongs praise.”

segments.arabic: قال عبد الله ولك الحمد
segments.english: ‘Abdullah said: “And to You belongs praise.”

segments.arabic: ثم يكبر حين يهوي ثم يكبر حين يرفع رأسه ثم يكبر حين يسجد ثم يكبر حين يرفع رأسه ثم يفعل ذلك في الصلاة كلها حتى يقضيها ويكبر حين يقوم من الثنتين بعد الجلوس
segments.english: Then he would say the takbir as he went down, then say the takbir as he raised his head, then say the takbir as he prostrated, then say the takbir as he raised his head. He would then do this throughout the prayer until he completed it. He would say the takbir when he stood after the two rak‘ahs, after sitting.

segments.arabic: [757] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي يعفور قال: سمعت مصعب بن سعد يقول
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Ya‘fur, who said: I heard Mus‘ab ibn Sa‘d say:

segments.arabic: صليت إلى جنب أبي فطبقت بين كفي ثم وضعتهما بين فخذي فنهاني أبي، وقال كنا نفعله فنهينا عنه وأمرنا أن نضع أيدينا على الركب
segments.english: I prayed beside my father, pressed my palms together, then put them between my thighs. My father forbade me and said, “We used to do it, then we were forbidden to do it and commanded to put our hands on our knees.”

notes: The source says between my thighs, not the knees wording of the Khan-family comparison. The final passive statements do not explicitly name who forbade or commanded; a parenthetical attribution is not added.

segments.arabic: [758] حدثنا حفص بن عمر قال: حدثنا شعبة عن سليمان قال: سمعت زيد بن وهب قال
segments.english: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sulayman, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb say:

segments.arabic: رأى حذيفة رجلا لا يتم الركوع والسجود قال: ما صليت ولو مت مت على غير الفطرة التي فطر الله محمدا ﷺ

segments.english: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: al-Hakam informed me, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara’, who said:

segments.arabic: [760] حدثنا مسدد قال: أخبرني يحيى بن سعيد عن عبيد الله قال: حدثنا سعيد المقبري عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id informed me, from ‘Ubaydullah, who said: Sa‘id al-Maqburi related to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ دخل المسجد فدخل رجل فصلى ثم جاء فسلم على النبي ﷺ فرد النبي ﷺ عليه السلام، فقال ارجع فصل فإنك لم تصل فصلى ثم جاء فسلم على النبي ﷺ، فقال ارجع فصل فإنك لم تصل ثلاثا، فقال والذي بعثك بالحق فما أحسن غيره فعلمني قال إذا قمت إلى الصلاة فكبر ثم اقرأ ما تيسر معك من القرآن ثم اركع حتى تطمئن راكعا ثم ارفع حتى تعتدل قائما ثم اسجد حتى تطمئن ساجدا ثم ارفع حتى تطمئن جالسا ثم اسجد حتى تطمئن ساجدا ثم افعل ذلك في صلاتك كلها
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the mosque. A man entered and prayed, then came and greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, returned his greeting and said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed.” He prayed, then came and greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed”—three times. He said, “By Him who sent you with the truth, I do not know how to do otherwise, so teach me.” He said, “When you stand for prayer, say the takbir, then recite what is easy for you of the Quran. Then bow until you are at rest in bowing, then rise until you are upright in standing. Then prostrate until you are at rest in prostration, then rise until you are at rest in sitting, then prostrate until you are at rest in prostration. Then do that throughout your prayer.”

notes: All four selected honorifics, both stated returns, the three-times expression and the second prostration remain. Informed me and related to us follow the selected digital and modern print readings; the historical print differs in those transmission verbs. No extra full trip is invented to expand three times.

segments.arabic: [761] حدثنا حفص بن عمر قال: حدثنا شعبة عن منصور عن أبي الضحى عن مسروق عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يقول: في ركوعه وسجوده سبحانك اللهم ربنا وبحمدك اللهم اغفر لي
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say in his bowing and prostration, “Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me.”

notes: The complete selected chain and the Most High wording in the companion honorific remain. The praise phrase is not replaced by an explanatory paraphrase.

segments.arabic: [762] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب عن سعيد المقبري عن أبي هريرة قال:
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ إذا قال سمع الله لمن حمده قال اللهم ربنا ولك الحمد وكان النبي ﷺ إذا ركع وإذا رفع رأسه يكبر وإذا قام من السجدتين قال الله أكبر
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” he said, “O Allah, our Lord, and to You belongs praise.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would say the takbir when he bowed and when he raised his head. When he rose from the two prostrations, he said, “Allah is greatest.”

notes: The selected Allahumma is retained although the English comparison wording omits it. The Arabic says two prostrations; it is not silently replaced by two rakahs. Both honorifics and the conjunction and in the praise response remain.

segments.arabic: [763] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن سمي عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إذا قال الإمام سمع الله لمن حمده فقولوا اللهم ربنا لك الحمد فإنه من وافق قوله قول الملائكة غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When the imam says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs praise.’ Whoever’s words coincide with the words of the angels will have his previous sins forgiven.”

notes: The selected and modern print praise response has no conjunction before to You; the historical print includes it. The selected response remains distinct from 762.

segments.arabic: [764] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة قال
segments.english: Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: لأقربن صلاة النبي ﷺ فكان أبو هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه يقنت في الركعة الأخرى من صلاة الظهر وصلاة العشاء وصلاة الصبح بعد ما يقول سمع الله لمن حمده فيدعو للمؤمنين ويلعن الكفار
segments.english: “I will certainly approximate the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, used to perform qunut in the last rak‘ah of the noon prayer, the night prayer and the dawn prayer, after saying, “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” He would supplicate for the believers and curse the unbelievers.

comparisons.note: The pinned EPUB goes directly from the imam’s praise response (1.12.762) to Anas on qunut in Maghrib and Fajr (1.12.763). Abu Hurayrah’s practice in this selected report is absent between those checked adjacent records. Bewley 764 and both Arabic prints contain it. This is a local checked absence, not a claim about every English edition.

notes: The emphatic future form is retained instead of changing it to a present-tense comparison. The subsequent practice remains attributed to Abu Hurayrah. The report is absent between the two checked adjacent Khan-family records; Bewley and both Arabic prints contain it. Chapter 44 is untitled in the selected source and modern print; the historical print adds a qunut title, which is not imported.

segments.arabic: [765] حدثنا عبد الله بن أبي الأسود قال: حدثنا إسماعيل عن خالد الحذاء عن أبي قلابة عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha’, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: كان القنوت في المغرب والفجر

segments.arabic: [766] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن نعيم بن عبد الله المجمر عن علي بن يحيى بن خلاد الزرقي عن أبيه عن رفاعة بن رافع الزرقي قال
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Nu‘aym ibn ‘Abdullah al-Mujmir, from ‘Ali ibn Yahya ibn Khallad al-Zuraqi, from his father, from Rifa‘ah ibn Rafi‘ al-Zuraqi, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا يوما نصلي وراء النبي ﷺ فلما رفع رأسه من الركعة قال سمع الله لمن حمده قال رجل وراءه ربنا ولك الحمد حمدا كثيرا طيبا مباركا فيه فلما انصرف قال من المتكلم قال: أنا قال: رأيت بضعة وثلاثين ملكا يبتدرونها أيهم يكتبها أول
segments.english: One day we were praying behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When he raised his head from bowing, he said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” A man behind him said, “Our Lord, and to You belongs praise—abundant, good, blessed praise.” When he finished, he said, “Who spoke?” He said, “I did.” He said, “I saw thirty-odd angels racing for it, to see which of them would write it first.”

notes: Both inspected Arabic prints include كثيرا in the praise phrase; the selected digital paragraph omits it. The explicit correction preserves the original and cites both exact pages. Thirty-odd does not impose a precise count. The Khan-family comparison appends Abu Humayd chapter material after this report; that material is not part of this numbered hadith.

segments.arabic: [767] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة عن ثابت قال:
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Thabit, who said:

segments.arabic: كان أنس ينعت لنا صلاة النبي ﷺ فكان يصلي وإذا رفع رأسه من الركوع قام حتى نقول قد نسي
segments.english: Anas used to describe for us the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He would pray, and when he raised his head from bowing, he would stand until we would say, “He has forgotten.”

notes: The selected Anas name is not expanded from the historical print. Nothing is added after he has forgotten to specify what had been forgotten.

segments.arabic: [768] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة عن الحكم عن ابن أبي ليلى عن البراء رضى الله تعالى عنه قال:
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara’, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: كان ركوع النبي ﷺ وسجوده وإذا رفع رأسه من الركوع وبين السجدتين قريبا من السواء
segments.english: The bowing of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his prostration, when he raised his head from bowing and the interval between the two prostrations were approximately equal.

notes: Approximately is retained, rather than the exact equality in the Khan-family comparison. The standing-and-sitting exception found in 759 is absent here and is not inserted.

segments.arabic: [769] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة قال:
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان مالك بن الحويرث يرينا كيف كان صلاة النبي ﷺ وذاك في غير وقت صلاة فقام فأمكن القيام ثم ركع فأمكن الركوع ثم رفع رأسه فأنصب هنية فصلى بنا صلاة شيخنا هذا أبي بريد وكان أبو بريد إذا رفع رأسه من السجدة الآخرة استوى قاعدا ثم نهض
segments.english: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith used to show us how the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was, and that was outside a prayer time. He stood and settled in the standing position, then bowed and settled in bowing, then raised his head and stood upright for a little while. He led us in a prayer like that of this shaykh of ours, Abu Burayd. When Abu Burayd raised his head from the last prostration, he sat upright, then rose.

notes: The selected digital and modern print name is Abu Burayd; the historical print and both English comparisons have Abu Yazid. The selected name is retained with a visible variant notice, not silently corrected. The selected فأنصب differs from printed فانتصب; the working English renders standing upright. Last prostration remains although the modern print omits last. The selected prayer time is not restricted to obligatory prayer.

segments.arabic: [770] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: حدثنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني أبو بكر ابن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb related to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed me:

segments.arabic: أن أبا هريرة كان يكبر في كل صلاة من المكتوبة وغيرها في رمضان وغيره فيكبر حين يقوم ثم يكبر حين يركع ثم يقول سمع الله لمن حمده ثم يقول ربنا ولك الحمد قبل أن يسجد ثم يقول الله أكبر حين يهوي ساجدا ثم يكبر حين يرفع رأسه من السجود ثم يكبر حين يسجد ثم يكبر حين يرفع رأسه من السجود ثم يكبر حين يقوم من الجلوس في الاثنتين ويفعل ذلك في كل ركعة حتى يفرغ من الصلاة ثم يقول حين ينصرف والذي نفسي بيده إني لأقربكم شبها بصلاة رسول الله ﷺ إن كانت هذه لصلاته حتى فارق الدنيا
segments.english: Abu Hurayrah used to say the takbir in every prayer, obligatory and otherwise, in Ramadan and otherwise. He would say the takbir when he stood, then say the takbir when he bowed, then say, “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” Then he would say, “Our Lord, and to You belongs praise,” before prostrating. Then he would say, “Allah is greatest,” as he went down in prostration, then say the takbir as he raised his head from prostration, then say the takbir as he prostrated, then say the takbir as he raised his head from prostration, then say the takbir as he stood from sitting after the two rak‘ahs. He would do that in every rak‘ah until he finished the prayer. Then, when he finished, he would say, “By Him in whose hand is my soul, my prayer resembles the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more closely than that of any of you. This was indeed his prayer until he left this world.”

segments.arabic: [771] قالا، وقال أبو هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: Both of them said: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, also said:

segments.arabic: وكان رسول الله ﷺ حين يرفع رأسه يقول سمع الله لمن حمده ربنا ولك الحمد يدعو لرجال فيسميهم بأسمائهم فيقول اللهم أنج الوليد بن الوليد وسلمة بن هشام وعياش بن أبي ربيعة والمستضعفين من المؤمنين اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر واجعلها عليهم سنين كسني يوسف
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his head, he would say, “Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.” He would supplicate for men, naming them by their names, saying, “O Allah, rescue al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah and the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, make Your grip severe upon Mudar, and make it years upon them like the years of Yusuf.”

segments.arabic: وأهل المشرق يومئذ من مضر مخالفون له
segments.english: At that time the people of the east, who were from Mudar, were opposing him.

comparisons.note: The pinned reference 1.12.768 combines Abu Hurayrah’s takbirs and the following named supplication. This part identifies only its corresponding complete selected report.

notes: The opening both continues the two informants in 770; a separate link supplies that context without inserting a repeated chain into this report. Abi in Ayyash ibn Abi Rabiah remains despite its omission in Bewley. Famine is not inserted into the selected years of Yusuf phrase. The closing historical statement remains separate from the quoted supplication. This is part two of Khan-family reference 1.12.768.

segments.arabic: [772] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان غير مرة عن الزهري قال: سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us more than once, from al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

segments.arabic: سقط رسول الله ﷺ عن فرس
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell from a horse.

segments.arabic: وربما قال سفيان من فرس
segments.english: Sometimes Sufyan said, “From a horse.”

segments.arabic: فجحش شقه الأيمن فدخلنا عليه نعوده فحضرت الصلاة فصلى بنا قاعدا وقعدنا،
segments.english: His right side was grazed. We went in to visit him. The time for prayer came, and he led us in prayer sitting, and we sat.

segments.arabic: وقال سفيان مرة صلينا قعودا
segments.english: On one occasion Sufyan said, “We prayed sitting.”

segments.arabic: فلما قضى الصلاة قال إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فإذا كبر فكبروا وإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا رفع فارفعوا وإذا قال سمع الله لمن حمده فقولوا ربنا ولك الحمد وإذا سجد فاسجدوا
segments.english: When he finished the prayer, he said, “The imam has only been appointed to be followed. When he says the takbir, say the takbir; when he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; when he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, and to You belongs praise’; and when he prostrates, prostrate.”

segments.arabic: قال سفيان كذا جاء به معمر قلت: نعم قال لقد حفظ كذا قال الزهري ولك الحمد حفظت من شقه الأيمن فلما خرجنا من عند الزهري قال ابن جريج وأنا عنده فجحش ساقه الأيمن
segments.english: Sufyan said, “Is that how Ma‘mar related it?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “He remembered it well.” That is how al-Zuhri said it: “And to You belongs praise.” I remembered “from his right side.” When we left al-Zuhri, Ibn Jurayj said—and I was with him—“His right leg was grazed.”

notes: Every interleaved variant and the full closing exchange remain. The Arabic prepositions عن and من both naturally render from in English; the repeated English phrase is deliberate, not a duplicate to remove. Both inspected prints have forearm in the closing variant, while the digital source has leg; al-Qastallani also records leg. The selected reading remains unchanged. The closing I and him are not replaced by invented narrator names where the attribution has been discussed differently.

segments.arabic: [773] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني سعيد بن المسيب وعطاء بن يزيد الليثي أن أبا هريرة أخبرهما
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid al-Laythi informed me that Abu Hurayrah informed them both:

segments.arabic: أن الناس قالوا يا رسول الله هل نرى ربنا يوم القيامة قال هل تمارون في القمر ليلة البدر ليس دونه حجاب قالوا لا يا رسول الله قال: فهل تمارون في الشمس ليس دونها سحاب قالوا لا قال: فإنكم ترونه كذلك يحشر الناس يوم القيامة فيقول من كان يعبد شيئا فليتبع فمنهم من يتبع الشمس ومنهم من يتبع القمر ومنهم من يتبع الطواغيت وتبقى هذه الأمة فيها منافقوها فيأتيهم الله فيقول أنا ربكم فيقولون هذا مكاننا حتى يأتينا ربنا فإذا جاء ربنا عرفناه فيأتيهم الله فيقول أنا ربكم فيقولون أنت ربنا فيدعوهم فيضرب الصراط بين ظهراني جهنم فأكون أول من يجوز من الرسل بأمته ولا يتكلم يومئذ أحد إلا الرسل وكلام الرسل يومئذ اللهم سلم سلم
segments.english: The people said, “Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?” He said, “Do you doubt the moon on the night of the full moon when there is no veil before it?” They said, “No, Messenger of Allah.” He said, “Do you doubt the sun when there is no cloud before it?” They said, “No.” He said, “You will see Him in that way. The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say, ‘Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it.’ Some of them will follow the sun, some will follow the moon, and some will follow false gods. This community will remain, with its hypocrites among it. Allah will come to them and say, ‘I am your Lord.’ They will say, ‘This is our place until our Lord comes to us. When our Lord comes, we will recognise Him.’ Allah will come to them and say, ‘I am your Lord.’ They will say, ‘You are our Lord.’ He will call them, and the bridge will be set across the midst of Hell. I will be the first of the messengers to cross with his community. No one will speak that day except the messengers, and the words of the messengers that day will be, ‘O Allah, grant safety, grant safety.’

segments.arabic: وفي جهنم كلاليب مثل شوك السعدان هل رأيتم شوك السعدان قالوا نعم قال: فإنها مثل شوك السعدان غير أنه لا يعلم قدر عظمها إلا الله تخطف الناس بأعمالهم فمنهم من يوبق بعمله ومنهم من يخردل ثم ينجو حتى إذا أراد الله رحمة من أراد من أهل النار أمر الله الملائكة أن يخرجوا من كان يعبد الله فيخرجونهم ويعرفونهم بآثار السجود وحرم الله على النار أن تأكل أثر السجود فيخرجون من النار فكل بن آدم تأكله النار إلا أثر السجود فيخرجون من النار قد امتحشوا فيصب عليهم ماء الحياة فينبتون كما تنبت الحبة في حميل السيل
segments.english: “In Hell there are hooks like the thorns of al-sa‘dan. Have you seen the thorns of al-sa‘dan?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “They are like the thorns of al-sa‘dan, except that no one knows how large they are but Allah. They snatch people according to their deeds. Among them are those ruined by their deeds, and among them are those cut to pieces who then escape. When Allah wishes to have mercy on whomever He wishes among the people of the Fire, Allah commands the angels to bring out those who used to worship Allah. They bring them out and recognise them by the marks of prostration. Allah has forbidden the Fire to consume the mark of prostration. They come out of the Fire. The Fire consumes all of the son of Adam except the mark of prostration. They come out of the Fire charred, and the water of life is poured over them. They grow as a seed grows in the silt carried by a flood.

segments.arabic: ثم يفرغ الله من القضاء بين العباد ويبقى رجل بين الجنة والنار وهو آخر أهل النار دخولا الجنة مقبل بوجهه قبل النار فيقول يا رب اصرف وجهي عن النار قد قشبني ريحها وأحرقني ذكاؤها فيقول هل عسيت إن فعل ذلك بك أن تسأل غير ذلك فيقول لا وعزتك فيعطي الله ما يشاء من عهد وميثاق فيصرف الله وجهه عن النار فإذا أقبل به على الجنة رأى بهجتها سكت ما شاء الله أن يسكت، ثم قال: يا رب قدمني عند باب الجنة فيقول الله له أليس قد أعطيت العهود والميثاق أن لا تسأل غير الذي كنت سألت فيقول يا رب لا أكون أشقى خلقك فيقول فما عسيت إن أعطيت ذلك أن لا تسأل غيره فيقول لا وعزتك لا أسأل غير ذلك فيعطي ربه ما شاء من عهد وميثاق فيقدمه إلى باب الجنة
segments.english: “Then Allah finishes judging between the servants. A man remains between the Garden and the Fire, and he is the last of the people of the Fire to enter the Garden. His face is turned towards the Fire. He says, ‘My Lord, turn my face away from the Fire. Its smell has poisoned me and its blaze has burned me.’ He says, ‘If that were done for you, might you ask for something else?’ He says, ‘No, by Your might.’ He gives Allah whatever pledge and covenant He wishes, and Allah turns his face away from the Fire. When He turns him towards the Garden, he sees its beauty and remains silent as long as Allah wishes him to remain silent. Then he says, ‘My Lord, bring me near the gate of the Garden.’ Allah says to him, ‘Have you not given pledges and a covenant that you would not ask for anything other than what you had asked for?’ He says, ‘My Lord, may I not be the most wretched of Your creation.’ He says, ‘If you were given that, would you not ask for something else?’ He says, ‘No, by Your might, I will not ask for anything else.’ He gives his Lord whatever pledge and covenant He wishes, and He brings him near the gate of the Garden.

segments.arabic: فإذا بلغ بابها فرأى زهرتها وما فيها من النضرة والسرور فيسكت ما شاء الله أن يسكت فيقول يا رب أدخلني الجنة فيقول الله ويحك يا ابن آدم ما أغدرك أليس قد أعطيت العهد والميثاق أن لا تسأل غير الذي أعطيت فيقول يا رب لا تجعلني أشقى خلقك فيضحك الله عز وجل منه ثم يأذن له في دخول الجنة فيقول تمن فيتمنى حتى إذا انقطعت أمنيته قال الله عز وجل من كذا وكذا أقبل يذكره ربه حتى إذا انتهت به الأماني قال الله تعالى لك ذلك ومثله معه
segments.english: “When he reaches its gate and sees its splendour and the freshness and joy within it, he remains silent as long as Allah wishes him to remain silent. He says, ‘My Lord, admit me to the Garden.’ Allah says, ‘Alas for you, son of Adam! How treacherous you are! Have you not given a pledge and covenant that you would not ask for anything other than what you were given?’ He says, ‘My Lord, do not make me the most wretched of Your creation.’ Allah, mighty and majestic, laughs at him, then permits him to enter the Garden. He says, ‘Wish.’ He wishes until, when his wishes cease, Allah, mighty and majestic, says, ‘Of such and such.’ His Lord begins reminding him, until, when his wishes come to an end, Allah Most High says, ‘You shall have that and the like of it with it.’”

segments.arabic: قال أبو سعيد الخدري لأبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: قال الله لك ذلك وعشرة أمثاله قال أبو هريرة لم أحفظ من رسول الله ﷺ إلا قوله لك ذلك ومثله معه قال أبو سعيد إني سمعته يقول ذلك لك وعشرة أمثاله
segments.english: Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said to Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Allah said, “You shall have that and ten times its like.” Abu Hurayrah said, “I remember nothing from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, except his saying, ‘You shall have that and the like of it with it.’” Abu Sa‘id said, “I heard him say, ‘You shall have that and ten times its like.’”

notes: The whole report remains one numbered entry; contiguous paragraph divisions do not create abridgements or session breakpoints. The digital moon clause says veil while both prints say cloud; the selected wording remains. Theological wording is retained without inserting an interpretive paraphrase. The working lexical choices cut to pieces, charred, flood-carried silt, poisoned and blaze follow the Arabic terms rather than additional explanations in the English comparisons. All repeated statements about coming out of the Fire remain. The selected elliptical من كذا وكذا has no command verb; the historical print adds زد, which is not inserted. The two companion recollections at the close remain distinct, including both honorifics.

segments.arabic: [774] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثني بكر بن مضر عن جعفر عن ابن هرمز عن عبد الله بن مالك بن بحينة
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Bakr ibn Mudar related to me, from Ja‘far, from Ibn Hurmuz, from ‘Abdullah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا صلى فرج بين يديه حتى يبدو بياض إبطيه،
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed, he spread his arms apart until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.

segments.arabic: وقال الليث حدثني جعفر بن ربيعة نحوه
segments.english: Al-Layth said: Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah related to me something similar.

notes: The selected short Yahya ibn Bukayr name is not expanded from the historical print. The complete closing al-Layth–Jafar ibn Rabiah attribution remains, although abbreviated or absent in the English comparisons.

segments.arabic: [775] حدثنا الصلت بن محمد قال: حدثنا مهدي عن واصل عن أبي وائل عن حذيفة
segments.english: Al-Salt ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Mahdi related to us, from Wasil, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah:

segments.arabic: رأى رجلا لا يتم ركوعه ولا سجوده فلما قضى صلاته قال له حذيفة ما صليت
segments.english: He saw a man who did not complete his bowing or his prostration. When he finished his prayer, Hudhayfah said to him, “You have not prayed.”

segments.arabic: قال وأحسبه قال ولو مت مت على غير سنة محمد ﷺ
segments.english: He said: I think he said, “If you had died, you would have died upon something other than the sunnah of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: The third-person framing and I think uncertainty remain. The short Mahdi name is not expanded from the historical print. Sunnah is not replaced by fitrah from the separate earlier report 758.

segments.arabic: [776] حدثنا قبيصة قال: حدثنا سفيان عن عمرو بن دينار عن طاوس عن ابن عباس
segments.english: Qabisah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

segments.arabic: أمر النبي ﷺ أن يسجد على سبعة أعضاء ولا يكف شعرا ولا ثوبا الجبهة واليدين والركبتين والرجلين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to prostrate on seven members and not to tuck up hair or clothing: the forehead, the two hands, the two knees and the two feet.

notes: Both inspected vocalised prints support was commanded. The source does not explicitly name the commander; no parenthetical attribution is inserted. Neither nose nor toes is added to the selected list. Hair precedes clothing, unlike the following report.

segments.arabic: [777] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا شعبة عن عمرو عن طاوس عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Amr, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: أمرنا أن نسجد على سبعة أعظم ولا نكف ثوبا ولا شعرا
segments.english: We were commanded to prostrate on seven bones and not to tuck up clothing or hair.

notes: The selected short Amr name is not expanded. The passive command, bones wording, dual companion honorific and clothing-before-hair order remain.

segments.arabic: [778] حدثنا آدم حدثنا إسرائيل عن أبي إسحاق عن عبد الله بن يزيد الخطمي حدثنا البراء بن عازب وهو غير كذوب قال
segments.english: Adam related to us. Isra’il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Khatmi: al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib related to us—and he was not a liar—saying:

segments.arabic: كنا نصلي خلف النبي ﷺ فإذا قال سمع الله لمن حمده لم يحن أحد منا ظهره حتى يضع النبي ﷺ جبهته على الأرض
segments.english: We used to pray behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When he said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” none of us would bend his back until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, placed his forehead on the ground.

notes: Related to us follows the selected and modern print; the historical print has related to me for Israil. The narrator qualification he was not a liar remains. Both honorifics and forehead are retained without adding nose.
